templates.display_name: Rideshare trips and fares per pickup zone and day (lake)
templates.description: Reads the pre-aggregated hvfhv_zone_day table straight out of the dp-lake object store - Parquet on S3, queried in place, nothing downloaded. One row per pickup zone and day, summed across Uber, Lyft, Via and Juno. The table is already at (zone, day, company) grain, so this node reads a few hundred thousand rows rather than the 400M-row trip table beside it. Expects INTEGER parameters year and month (1-12); the month's bounds are derived in DuckDB (make_date and last_day), so the door is the month the question names, never two dates. The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024.
templates.body:
SELECT
    r.pickup_date                     AS pickup_date,
    r.pu_location_id                  AS pu_location_id,
    SUM(r.trip_count)                 AS rideshare_trips,
    ROUND(SUM(r.total_base_fare), 2)  AS rideshare_base_fare,
    SUM(r.shared_request_count)       AS rideshare_shared_requests
FROM hvfhv_zone_day r
WHERE r.pickup_date BETWEEN make_date(:year, :month, 1) AND last_day(make_date(:year, :month, 1))
GROUP BY r.pickup_date, r.pu_location_id

templates.display_name: Yellow-taxi trips and fares per pickup zone and day
templates.description: Trip-level scan of the sample-trips Postgres database at (day, pickup zone) grain - the same grain the lake node returns, so the two engines' rows line up without either side being re-aggregated. The raw TLC feed carries implausible rows, so this node keeps only 0 < distance < 100 miles and 0 < total < 1000 USD, which is what makes an average a fact rather than an artifact of one bad row. Expects INTEGER parameters year and month (1-12); the month's bounds are derived in Postgres (make_date plus one month). The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024; one month keeps the trip-level scan at a few seconds.
templates.body:
SELECT
    t.pickup_date                 AS pickup_date,
    t.pu_location_id              AS pu_location_id,
    COUNT(*)                      AS taxi_trips,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_amount), 2) AS taxi_total_amount
FROM trips t
WHERE t.pickup_date >= make_date(:year, :month, 1)
  AND t.pickup_date <  (make_date(:year, :month, 1) + INTERVAL '1 month')::date
  AND t.trip_distance_mi > 0 AND t.trip_distance_mi < 100
  AND t.total_amount     > 0 AND t.total_amount     < 1000
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pu_location_id

templates.display_name: TLC taxi zones and boroughs (for the lake showcase)
templates.description: Reads the 265-row zone lookup from the sample-reference SQLite datasource. Takes no parameters. The two catch-all zones ('Unknown' and 'N/A') are excluded so a borough rollup has no bucket that is not a borough. Both the taxi table and the lake table carry the same TLC zone ids, which is why one lookup serves both.
templates.body:
SELECT
    z.location_id AS location_id,
    z.borough     AS borough,
    z.zone        AS zone_name
FROM zones z
WHERE z.borough NOT IN ('Unknown', 'N/A')

templates.display_name: Daily precipitation, averaged across the NYC stations
templates.description: One row per day from the sample-weather MySQL database with precipitation in millimetres, averaged across the five NYC-area stations. Days with no PRCP reading anywhere come back NULL and are treated as dry by the answer node. Expects INTEGER parameters year and month (1-12); the month's bounds are derived in MySQL (MAKEDATE plus months). The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024.
templates.body:
SELECT
    o.obs_date                                                   AS obs_date,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN o.element = 'PRCP' THEN o.value END), 2) AS precip_mm
FROM observations o
WHERE o.obs_date >= MAKEDATE(:year, 1) + INTERVAL (:month - 1) MONTH
  AND o.obs_date <  MAKEDATE(:year, 1) + INTERVAL :month MONTH
  AND o.element = 'PRCP'
GROUP BY o.obs_date

templates.display_name: Rain lift per borough: taxi vs rideshare
templates.description: The answer node. Puts the four staged tables together in tempdb: yellow-taxi zone-days from Postgres, rideshare zone-days from the lake, the borough lookup from SQLite and the day's rainfall from MySQL. The two trip sources are UNIONed to a common grain before aggregation rather than joined, so a zone-day that only one of them saw still counts - an inner join between them would silently drop it and every rate on the screen would be wrong by a few points. stg_taxi is a 1-in-16 hash sample (sources.lock: trips_sample_modulus 16) while stg_rideshare is the full census, so a taxi/rideshare share would be a number about the sampling, not the city — the deliverable is the per-mode RAIN LIFT (rainy per-day trips / dry per-day trips, per borough), a within-mode ratio in which the sample rate cancels, and the raw per-day columns are labelled ‘sampled’ so nobody reads them as totals. Binds :rain_threshold_mm, :year and :month (declared parameters); the month's length is derived in H2 from year and month, in the window_days CTE, and every per-day rate divides by it. The weather bucket is computed in an inner CTE so the outer GROUP BY names plain columns — H2's matching of two parameterized CASE expressions is data-dependent (089 live gate).
templates.body:
WITH grain AS (
    SELECT t.pickup_date AS d, t.pu_location_id AS z,
           t.taxi_trips  AS taxi_trips, 0 AS rideshare_trips
    FROM stg_taxi t
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.pickup_date, r.pu_location_id,
           0, r.rideshare_trips
    FROM stg_rideshare r
),
bucketed AS (
    SELECT
        z.borough                                                                AS borough,
        CASE WHEN COALESCE(w.precip_mm, 0) >= :rain_threshold_mm THEN 'rainy' ELSE 'dry' END AS weather,
        g.taxi_trips                                                             AS taxi_trips,
        g.rideshare_trips                                                        AS rideshare_trips
    FROM grain g
    JOIN stg_zones z ON z.location_id = g.z
    LEFT JOIN stg_rain w ON w.obs_date = g.d
)
,
window_days AS (
    -- The month's length, from the same year/month door the source nodes bound: H2 date
    -- arithmetic from the two integers, so every per-day rate divides by the window.
    SELECT DAY_OF_MONTH(LAST_DAY(DATEADD('MONTH', :month - 1, DATEADD('YEAR', :year - 1970, DATE '1970-01-01')))) AS n
),
per_day AS (
    SELECT
        borough                                                                 AS borough,
        weather                                                                 AS weather,
        CAST(SUM(taxi_trips) AS DECIMAL(18,4))
            / (SELECT n FROM window_days)                                  AS taxi_per_day,
        CAST(SUM(rideshare_trips) AS DECIMAL(18,4))
            / (SELECT n FROM window_days)                                  AS rideshare_per_day
    FROM bucketed
    GROUP BY borough, weather
)
SELECT
    borough                                                                       AS borough,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'dry'   THEN taxi_per_day END), 1)             AS taxi_sampled_trips_per_day_dry,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'rainy' THEN taxi_per_day END), 1)             AS taxi_sampled_trips_per_day_rainy,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'dry'   THEN rideshare_per_day END), 1)        AS rideshare_trips_per_day_dry,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'rainy' THEN rideshare_per_day END), 1)        AS rideshare_trips_per_day_rainy,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'rainy' THEN taxi_per_day END)
          / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'dry' THEN taxi_per_day END), 0), 2)  AS taxi_rain_lift,
    ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'rainy' THEN rideshare_per_day END)
          / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN weather = 'dry' THEN rideshare_per_day END), 0), 2) AS rideshare_rain_lift
FROM per_day
GROUP BY borough
ORDER BY borough

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/taxi_vs_rideshare
pipelines.display_name: Rain lift: taxi vs rideshare, by borough
pipelines.description:
Question
Do New Yorkers switch to a taxi, or to a rideshare, when it rains? One row per borough: sampled taxi trips per day and rideshare trips per day on dry and on rainy days, and each mode's RAIN LIFT (its rainy per-day figure over its dry one).

Window and door
One calendar month, chosen by year and month (default 2024, 12: December). The rainy threshold is rain_threshold_mm (default 2.5 mm, the US National Weather Service 'light rain' floor). Every source template derives the month's bounds in its own dialect - Postgres, DuckDB and MySQL each in their own date functions - and the answer node derives the month's length in H2 from the same two integers.

Sources and grain
FOUR ENGINES, one of them a data lake read in place. sample-trips (Postgres): trips, a deterministic 1-in-16 hash sample of yellow-taxi trips, rolled up at the source to one row per (day, pickup zone). sample-lake (DuckDB over Parquet on S3, nothing downloaded): hvfhv_zone_day, the FULL census of Uber/Lyft/Via/Juno trips at (day, pickup zone, company) grain, summed over companies - the 400M-row trip table beside it is never touched. sample-reference (SQLite): zones, the TLC lookup both trip tables share. sample-weather (MySQL): observations, five stations averaged to one PRCP value per day.

Interpretation
The taxi side is a sample and the rideshare side a census, so a taxi/rideshare SHARE would be a number about the sampling, not the city; the deliverable is the within-mode rain lift, a ratio in which the sample rate cancels, and the raw per-day taxi columns are labelled 'sampled' so nobody reads them as totals. A day is rainy at or above the threshold; no reading counts as dry. The two trip sources are UNIONed to a common (day, zone) grain before aggregation rather than joined, so a zone-day only one of them saw still counts. The plausibility filter (0 < miles < 100, 0 < total < 1000 USD) applies to the taxi rows at the source.

Verification
Lake total for the month, SELECT SUM(trip_count) FROM hvfhv_zone_day WHERE pickup_date BETWEEN '2024-12-01' AND '2024-12-31': 21,065,840 rideshare trips over 31 days. Multiplying every row's rideshare dry and rainy per-day figures by 31 and summing recovers 21,065,082.8 - the total within the rounding of the per-day figures. Rainy days in the month from the weather source (the same AVG(value) >= 2.5 query as rainy_vs_dry_ridership, over December): 11 of 31.

Caveats
The per-day figures divide each weather bucket's total by the window's 31 days, not by that bucket's own day count; with 11 rainy and 20 dry days in December 2024 the rain lift therefore compares the two buckets' TOTALS, and a lift near 11/20 (0.55) is what 'no effect' looks like. EWR is Newark Airport's zone, not a borough. Trip counts on the taxi side are sample counts (x16 for the population).

year.description: The calendar year to report, as the question names it (2024). The sample covers 2023 and 2024.

month.description: The month of that year to report, 1-12 (the default, 12, is December).

rain_threshold_mm.description: Millimetres of precipitation, averaged across the five stations, at or above which a day counts as rainy. 2.5 mm is the US National Weather Service's 'light rain' floor.

nodes.description: Stage the month's yellow-taxi trips per pickup zone and day from Postgres: one row per (day, pickup zone).

Stage the month's rideshare trips per pickup zone and day from the dp-lake object store: one row per (day, pickup zone), summed over companies. The datasource is read-only Parquet on S3: the pre-aggregate is a few hundred thousand rows, and the 400M-row trip table beside it is only touched by a query that names it.
Stage the taxi-zone lookup so both trip sources can be rolled up to boroughs.
Stage the month's average precipitation per day from MySQL: one row per day.
Join the four staged tables and report the rideshare share per borough, split by whether the day was rainy.
